name: Establishing Collaborative Therapeutic Relationship
description: Initiate and maintain a collaborative, supportive alliance characterized by empathy, warmth, and shared goal-setting.

goal.objective: Form a strong, trusting partnership between therapist and patient to enable engagement in CBT work.

success_levels.ideal: Patient feels understood, safe, motivated, and actively participates in setting therapy goals.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient is generally willing to engage, expresses some trust, and participates with occasional reservations.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient remains distant, disengaged, mistrustful, or resistant to therapy involvement.

goal.reward_hint: Observable patient engagement, disclosure, and willingness to collaborate on goals.

states: Patient is hesitant, anxious, or ambivalent about treatment
Beginning work with new patients or after ruptures in alliance

micro_actions.name: Greeting and Warm Welcome
micro_actions.description: Begin the session with a warm, friendly greeting, showing genuine interest in the patient’s well-being.

micro_actions.name: Reflect and Validate Patient Experience
micro_actions.description: Verbally reflect and validate the patient’s distress, concerns, or hopes, demonstrating empathy and understanding.

micro_actions.name: Solicit Collaborative Input
micro_actions.description: Ask open-ended questions about the patient’s preferences, goals, and expectations for therapy and invite input.

micro_actions.name: Share Session Structure Transparently
micro_actions.description: Explain session format and structure collaboratively, address questions or uncertainties.
states: When patient is unfamiliar with CBT

micro_actions.name: Empathic Responses to Patient Feedback
micro_actions.description: Acknowledge and respond supportively to patient feedback or concerns about therapy.
states: Patient provides feedback or voices concerns

name: Assessment and Case Formulation
description: Comprehensively assess presenting problems, symptoms, history, and use CBT concepts to develop a shared understanding and treatment plan.

goal.objective: Construct an individualized CBT case conceptualization to guide targeted interventions.

success_levels.ideal: Thorough, collaboratively developed case formulation guides precise and personalized treatment planning.
success_levels.acceptable: A basic formulation is created and referenced, though details may be lacking or incomplete.
success_levels.unsuccessful: No clear formulation, or one that is inaccurate, missing, or ignored in treatment.

goal.reward_hint: Patient and therapist reference conceptualization, plan interventions, and update hypotheses as needed.

states: When modifying treatment plan due to new information
Patient progress stalls or unexpected difficulties arise

micro_actions.name: Conduct Structured Symptom Inquiry
micro_actions.description: Ask targeted questions about current symptoms, triggers, and history using structured interviews and rating scales.

micro_actions.name: Administer Standardized Measures
micro_actions.description: Invite the patient to complete standardized self-report scales or questionnaires for symptoms and functioning.

micro_actions.name: Elicit Narrative History
micro_actions.description: Prompt the patient to narrate relevant past events, relationship patterns, and developmental influences with open-ended prompts.

micro_actions.name: Probe for Cognitive-Behavioral Patterns
micro_actions.description: Guide the patient to describe specific thoughts, emotions, and behaviors linked to problematic situations.

micro_actions.name: Collaborative Hypothesis Generation
micro_actions.description: Discuss and formulate preliminary working hypotheses about links between thoughts, emotions, behaviors, and underlying schemas.

name: Session Structuring and Agenda Setting
description: Actively structure CBT sessions by jointly setting an agenda to organize time around specific goals and actions.

goal.objective: Maximize session productivity, focus, and relevance through shared session organization.

success_levels.ideal: Agenda is collaboratively set, followed, and reviewed, with main priorities addressed and patient actively involved.
success_levels.acceptable: Agenda is loosely set and mostly followed, with some drift or unaddressed priorities.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Session is unfocused, agenda is absent or ignored, patient feels lost or dissatisfied.

goal.reward_hint: Session structure maps onto the patient's treatment goals and both parties refer to the agenda.

states: Patient appears scattered, overwhelmed, or unfocused
Therapy progress is drifting or patient feels dissatisfied

micro_actions.name: Initiate Collaborative Agenda Setting
micro_actions.description: Ask the patient what topics or goals they wish to discuss, add therapist recommendations, and jointly prioritize session items.

micro_actions.name: State and Clarify Agenda Items
micro_actions.description: Clearly verbalize session agenda items and ensure mutual understanding of their importance.

micro_actions.name: Redirect Discussion to Agenda
micro_actions.description: Politely steer off-topic conversation back to agreed-upon agenda items to maintain session focus.

micro_actions.name: Review and Summarize Agenda Completion
micro_actions.description: At session end, review progress on agenda items, and invite the patient to summarize what was addressed.

micro_actions.name: Provide Opportunity for Immediate Feedback
micro_actions.description: Solicit patient feedback about session flow, agenda balance, and relevance.

name: Psychoeducation
description: Teach CBT theory, techniques, and self-help strategies to empower and motivate the patient.

goal.objective: Increase patient's understanding of CBT and its relevance to their problems, enhancing engagement and efficacy.

success_levels.ideal: Patient demonstrates accurate understanding of CBT concepts and applies them effectively.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient shows partial understanding and applies concepts inconsistently.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient remains confused or rejects CBT concepts and interventions.

goal.reward_hint: Patient restates and uses CBT concepts in session and homework.

states: Patient expresses confusion, uncertainty, or skepticism toward CBT
When troubleshooting skill non-use or misapplication

micro_actions.name: Deliver Clear Explanations of CBT Concepts
micro_actions.description: Use concise, jargon-free language to verbally describe CBT theory and techniques with relevant examples.

micro_actions.name: Use Psychoeducational Materials in Session
micro_actions.description: Hand out or engage with worksheets, diagrams, or technology to illustrate concepts visually and interactively.

micro_actions.name: Model Completion of CBT Exercises
micro_actions.description: Verbally walk through an example of a CBT exercise such as a thought record, and openly share rationale and steps.

micro_actions.name: Solicit Patient Restatement and Teaching
micro_actions.description: Ask the patient to summarize in their own words what they've learned about CBT concepts.

micro_actions.name: Correct Misunderstandings Supportively
micro_actions.description: Gently clarify errors or misconceptions and encourage questions for deeper understanding.

name: Identification and Modification of Automatic Thoughts
description: Help patient uncover automatic thoughts influencing emotions and behavior, then employ cognitive strategies to challenge or restructure them.

goal.objective: Reduce negative affect and maladaptive behavior by reshaping dysfunctional thought patterns.

success_levels.ideal: Patient reliably identifies and modifies automatic thoughts, reporting symptom relief and functional improvement.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient sometimes identifies/modifies thoughts, with moderate improvements in mood or behavior.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient cannot identify or modify automatic thoughts; symptoms persist.

goal.reward_hint: Patient demonstrates ability to record, question, and reframe thoughts both in session and homework.

states: Patient reports distressing emotions or unhelpful behaviors
Difficulty understanding causes of current problems

micro_actions.name: Use Socratic Questioning to Elicit Automatic Thoughts
micro_actions.description: Ask open-ended, exploratory questions like 'What went through your mind in that moment?' or 'Can you describe your thoughts as the situation unfolded?'
states: Therapist is seeking the patient's thoughts

micro_actions.name: Prompt Patient to Record Thoughts and Feelings
micro_actions.description: Encourage the patient to use thought records or worksheets during and between sessions to log automatic thoughts and associated emotions.

micro_actions.name: Guide Evidence Examination
micro_actions.description: Ask the patient to identify evidence for and against their automatic thought and discuss the validity of each viewpoint.
states: Patient is stuck in negative cognitions

micro_actions.name: Identify and Label Cognitive Errors
micro_actions.description: Point out common cognitive distortions (e.g., catastrophizing, all-or-nothing thinking) when observed, giving clear explanations and examples.

micro_actions.name: Guide Generation of Rational Alternatives
micro_actions.description: Coach the patient to brainstorm alternative, more balanced or adaptive thoughts and write them down.

micro_actions.name: Rate Belief Strength and Emotional Change
micro_actions.description: Prompt the patient to rate how strongly they believe the automatic thought and how their emotions shift as they consider alternatives.

name: Behavioral Activation and Activity Scheduling
description: Encourage graded increases in pleasurable and mastery-oriented activities to improve mood and engagement.

goal.objective: Facilitate behavioral change that counters avoidance, improves mood, and increases motivation.

success_levels.ideal: Patient consistently engages in scheduled activities, reporting increased pleasure and accomplishment.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient participates in some activities with intermittent progress and partial symptom relief.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient avoids activities; mood and activity levels remain low or worsen.

goal.reward_hint: Patient completes and reflects on activity logs; reports increased well-being.

states: Patient presents with low energy, decreased pleasure, avoidance or withdrawal
Patient struggles with inactivity or lack of motivation

micro_actions.name: Collaborative Brainstorming of Activities
micro_actions.description: Ask the patient to suggest pleasurable and mastery activities and problem-solve barriers together.

micro_actions.name: Assign Specific, Measurable Activity Tasks
micro_actions.description: Help the patient schedule activities with concrete dates, times, and details, writing them down for accountability.

micro_actions.name: Review and Rate Completed Activities
micro_actions.description: Ask the patient to rate each activity for pleasure and mastery (e.g., 0–10 scale) and discuss mood changes.

micro_actions.name: Normalize Difficulty and Troubleshoot Noncompletion
micro_actions.description: Supportively acknowledge obstacles and brainstorm realistic solutions, avoiding blame and encouraging persistence.
states: Patient did not complete scheduled activity

micro_actions.name: Credit Partial Success and Encourage Use of Reminders
micro_actions.description: Give positive, nonjudgmental feedback for any engagement and suggest using notes, phone prompts, or external supports to increase follow-through.
states: Patient completed part but not all of assigned activity

name: Skills Training and Coping Skills Acquisition
description: Teach, coach, and rehearse skills including relaxation, problem-solving, emotion regulation, and coping strategies.

goal.objective: Enhance patient's repertoire of adaptive coping and emotional regulation techniques.

success_levels.ideal: Patient masters skills, applying them independently with sustained benefits.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient learns and occasionally applies some skills, with limited gain.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient does not use taught skills, remaining dysregulated and unable to cope.

goal.reward_hint: Patient demonstrates skills fluency in session and in real-life situations.

states: Patient displays poor coping, problematic emotional responses, or skill deficits
New technique needs to be introduced or reinforced
Patient asks for concrete tools or strategies

micro_actions.name: Teach Coping or Relaxation Technique
micro_actions.description: Explain and demonstrate step-by-step methods for relaxation (e.g., deep breathing, muscle tension release), problem-solving, or emotion regulation.
states: Patient reports stress or emotional difficulty

micro_actions.name: Coach Skill Practice in Session
micro_actions.description: Guide patient to rehearse the skill (e.g., breathing exercises, role-play) during the session, providing supportive feedback.

micro_actions.name: Assign Skills Practice for Homework
micro_actions.description: Give clear instructions for practice outside session (e.g., practice relaxation daily) and encourage written tracking.

micro_actions.name: Review and Troubleshoot Skill Use
micro_actions.description: Inquire about difficulties with skill application, collaboratively brainstorm solutions, and normalize setbacks.

micro_actions.name: Provide Positive and Specific Feedback
micro_actions.description: Recognize any effort or progress in skills use and give constructive feedback tailored to patient strengths.

name: Systematic Exposure and Response Prevention
description: Gradually expose patient to feared or avoided stimuli and prevent safety behaviors or rituals to reduce anxiety and avoidance.

goal.objective: Decrease anxiety and avoidance through habituation, extinction, and behavioral learning.

success_levels.ideal: Patient faces feared situations, eliminates avoidance, and reports significant anxiety reduction.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient partially completes exposures, with some decrease in distress.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient resists exposure, maintains avoidance, anxiety remains high.

goal.reward_hint: Patient completes assigned exposures and can report decreased distress over time.

states: Patient presents with anxiety, phobia, or OCD symptoms
High avoidance or ritualistic safety behaviors

micro_actions.name: Elicit and Record Avoided or Feared Situations
micro_actions.description: Ask the patient to list specific situations, objects, or activities that provoke anxiety or avoidance, and collaboratively rate difficulty.

micro_actions.name: Develop Exposure Hierarchy Collaboratively
micro_actions.description: Construct a graded list of anxiety-provoking tasks (8–12 steps), with patient input and ratings for expected anxiety.

micro_actions.name: Coach and Support Exposure Practice
micro_actions.description: Guide the patient through imaginal or in vivo exposure tasks in session or assign as homework, providing encouragement and feedback.

micro_actions.name: Monitor and Prevent Safety Behaviors
micro_actions.description: Ask about rituals, avoidance, or distraction strategies during exposures, and support patient in refraining from them.
states: Patient expresses urge for safety behaviors

micro_actions.name: Debrief and Reinforce Post-Exposure
micro_actions.description: Discuss patient experiences after exposure, reinforce adaptive behaviors, and reflect on anxiety changes.

name: Schema Identification and Modification
description: Identify, educate about, and collaboratively rework maladaptive core schemas using cognitive and behavioral strategies.

goal.objective: Restructure underlying maladaptive schemas to promote lasting change in self-concept and interpersonal functioning.

success_levels.ideal: Patient identifies and modifies core schemas, demonstrating healthier beliefs and behavior patterns.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient identifies some schemas with partial modification or inconsistent application.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient unable or unwilling to explore schemas; dysfunctional patterns persist.

goal.reward_hint: Patient can describe schemas, actively works to modify them, and reports life changes.

states: Automatic thoughts are rooted in core schema issues
Patient open to deeper cognitive work

micro_actions.name: Use Downward Arrow Technique
micro_actions.description: Ask recursive, probing questions (e.g., 'If that were true, what would it mean about you?') to uncover core beliefs.

micro_actions.name: Track Mood and Thought Patterns
micro_actions.description: Collaboratively observe and discuss patterns in mood shifts and recurring automatic thoughts for clues to schemas.

micro_actions.name: Use Schema Inventories or Thought Records
micro_actions.description: Direct the patient to complete schema assessments or record schema-driven thoughts in writing.

micro_actions.name: Examine Evidence for and Against Schema
micro_actions.description: Ask patient to identify and discuss evidence supporting or challenging the schema, and label cognitive errors.

micro_actions.name: Generate Alternative Schemas
micro_actions.description: Guide the patient to create alternative, more adaptive core beliefs and collaboratively list advantages/disadvantages.

micro_actions.name: Coach Cognitive/Behavioral Rehearsal
micro_actions.description: Engage the patient in practicing new schema-related behaviors and thoughts in role-play or homework.

name: Suicide Risk Assessment and Safety Planning
description: Assess suicide risk, foster hope and commitment to treatment, develop and review a structured safety plan to manage risk.

goal.objective: Reduce immediate risk of self-harm by increasing crisis safety, hope, and actionable coping plans.

success_levels.ideal: Patient fully engages with safety plan, demonstrates increased hope and reduced risk.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient participates in risk assessment and safety planning with guarded cooperation.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient refuses safety protocols; risk remains unmitigated.

goal.reward_hint: Patient commits to safety plan, identifies reasons for living, and implements crisis resources.

states: Patient expresses suicidal ideation, hopelessness, or past attempts
Major life crisis or elevated distress
Post-acute crisis or planning for discharge

micro_actions.name: Directly Assess Suicidal Ideation and Plans
micro_actions.description: Ask explicit, direct questions about suicidal thoughts, intent, plans, means, and prior attempts.

micro_actions.name: Administer Standardized Suicide Risk Measures
micro_actions.description: Invite the patient to complete measures such as PHQ-9 or BDI-II for baseline and ongoing risk tracking.

micro_actions.name: Collaboratively Develop Safety Plan
micro_actions.description: Stepwise construct a written safety plan: identify warning signs, coping strategies, crisis contacts, means restriction, and access to emergency help.

micro_actions.name: Expand Reasons for Living and Hope
micro_actions.description: Ask targeted questions to brainstorm and reinforce meaningful reasons for living, support construction of hope kits.

micro_actions.name: Troubleshoot Barriers to Safety Plan Execution
micro_actions.description: Discuss obstacles to safety plan steps and collaboratively generate solutions, revising plan as needed.

micro_actions.name: Review and Revise Safety Plan Regularly
micro_actions.description: At subsequent sessions, systematically review safety plan effectiveness, updating as appropriate.

name: Homework Assignment and Review
description: Assign, monitor, and troubleshoot between-session tasks to generalize skills and promote independent practice.

goal.objective: Increase skill uptake and real-world behavioral change through active practice and self-monitoring.

success_levels.ideal: Patient completes and reviews homework consistently, demonstrating transfer of skills to daily life.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient attempts homework with partial completion or engagement.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient avoids homework, shows minimal skill generalization.

goal.reward_hint: Patient brings in homework, discusses insights, shows progress outside sessions.

states: Session ends and new targets set
Patient displays difficulty applying skills between sessions

micro_actions.name: Assign Specific Homework Tasks
micro_actions.description: Clearly articulate homework assignments, including rationale, details, and written instructions for tracking and accountability.

micro_actions.name: Review Homework Completion and Insights
micro_actions.description: Inquire about patient experiences with homework, review content, and discuss insights or difficulties.

micro_actions.name: Troubleshoot Barriers to Homework
micro_actions.description: Explore reasons for incomplete homework, normalize difficulties, collaboratively problem-solve solutions.

micro_actions.name: Give Supportive Feedback on Practice
micro_actions.description: Acknowledge and reinforce patient effort and success in homework, avoiding judgment or criticism.

micro_actions.name: Collaboratively Adjust Homework Assignments
micro_actions.description: Negotiate assignment details and difficulty, eliminate impractical tasks, and write down changes for clarity.

name: Relapse Prevention Planning
description: Consolidate gains, anticipate relapse risks, teach maintenance and recovery strategies, and plan for post-treatment follow-up.

goal.objective: Prepare patient to sustain progress and cope with setbacks independently post-therapy.

success_levels.ideal: Patient is proactive about relapse prevention, uses maintenance strategies, and recovers from setbacks autonomously.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient understands relapse risks and uses some coping strategies though needs reminders.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient is unprepared for relapse; regression occurs with no recovery plan.

goal.reward_hint: Patient articulates, practices, and implements relapse prevention strategies.

states: Later stages of treatment approaching termination

micro_actions.name: Review Progress and Consolidate Gains
micro_actions.description: Discuss specific improvements and stabilized changes the patient has made, reinforcing strengths.

micro_actions.name: Identify Potential Relapse Triggers
micro_actions.description: Ask patient to list situations, thoughts, or feelings that may put progress at risk.

micro_actions.name: Teach and Model Maintenance Strategies
micro_actions.description: Explain, demonstrate, and collaboratively write out strategies for coping with setbacks, problem-solving, and self-monitoring.

micro_actions.name: Plan Post-Treatment Follow-Up
micro_actions.description: Discuss options and plans for continued monitoring, access to resources, and future booster sessions if needed.

name: Therapist Competence Monitoring and Supervision Engagement
description: Therapist actively monitors own CBT competence, seeks supervision and feedback, pursues professional learning, and self-care practices.

goal.objective: Ensure therapist maintains high skill level, ethical standards, and wellness for effective CBT delivery.

success_levels.ideal: Therapist regularly engages in self-reflection, supervision, and education, preventing burnout and maintaining competence.
success_levels.acceptable: Therapist intermittently reviews skills and seeks feedback, skills may stagnate.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Therapist neglects competence monitoring, leading to suboptimal care or burnout.

goal.reward_hint: Therapist documents supervision, self-assessment, and continuing learning activities.

states: Therapist is new, encounters complex/novel cases
Skill gaps or burnout are suspected
Periodic review of practice per guidelines

micro_actions.name: Self-Reflect on Session Competence
micro_actions.description: After each session, reflect verbally or via notes on use of CBT methods, strengths, and areas for improvement.

micro_actions.name: Seek and Integrate Supervisor Feedback
micro_actions.description: Regularly present cases and questions in supervision or peer review and act on feedback received.

micro_actions.name: Engage in Continuing Education
micro_actions.description: Attend trainings, complete CBT readings, review guidelines, and discuss learning points in meetings.

micro_actions.name: Monitor and Manage Own Wellness
micro_actions.description: Discuss personal stress, burnout signs, countertransference, and seek support/resources if needed.
